 1           Plaintiff Sierra Robinson (“Plaintiffs”), on behalf of herself and all others similarly situated

 2   (“Class Members”), by and through their attorneys of record, files this Class Action Complaint against

 3   Defendant Apple Inc.. (“Apple” or “Defendant”) a California Corporation alleging the following, based

 4   upon personal knowledge, where applicable, information and belief, and the investigation of counsel:

 5                                         NATURE OF THE ACTION

 6           1.      Defendant Apple Inc. is a California corporation with its principal place of business

 7   located at One Apple Park Way, Cupertino, California 95014.

 8           2.      Apple is a prominent technology company and manufacturer of smart cell phones,

 9   tablets, computers and other technology products.

10           3.      In addition to offering physical product for sale, Apple is a developer of artificial

11   intelligence platforms. One such platform is “Siri.” Siri is marketed as a digital assistant developed

12   and owned by Apple that integrates with its various operating systems.

13           4.      Apple has also the developer of Apple Intelligence which uses artificial intelligence to

14   enhance the use of Siri on its devices.

15           5.      Apple has numerous physical stores where it sells its products all over the United States

16   and also operates an online store on the internet. As such, Apple regularly conducts business throughout

17   California and in this judicial district.

18           6.      In September 2024, Apple released and began selling its iPhone 16 cell phone. Apple

19   promotes this product as the first phone built with Apple Intelligence.
20           7.      Apple launched an extensive, multi-platform marketing campaign for the iPhone 16,

21   heavily promoting its new “Apple Intelligence” AI features—especially enhanced Siri capabilities—as

22   revolutionary. Apple positioned these AI tools as the defining feature of the device, leading consumers

23   to reasonably expect that these innovations would be available at the time of release.

24           8.      Apple’s marketing generated unprecedented consumer excitement, helping justify

25   premium pricing and positioning the company as a leader in the AI race. However, Apple knew these

26   promoted AI features—especially the Siri enhancements—were not real, and only recently admitted

27   they were never available, following backlash and industry scrutiny.

28           9.      In 2024, Apple shipped 226 million phones worldwide.

                                           CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                     -1-
             Case 5:25-cv-04776-VKD           Document 1        Filed 06/05/25      Page 3 of 16




 1          10.     Apple’s false and deceptive marketing practices concerning the iPhone 16 allowed it to

 2   sell 11% more of this model than it sold the iPhone 15 in the previous year (2023).

 3          11.     Apple misled millions of consumers into buying new phones they didn’t need by

 4   promoting non-existent features, in clear violation of numerous false advertising and consumer

 5   protection laws.

 6                                                  PARTIES

 7   A.     Plaintiff

 8          12.     Plaintiff Sierra Robinson (“Plaintiff”) is a citizen of California, residing in the city of

 9   Los Angeles, in Los Angeles County, California.

10          13.     On December 2024, Plaintiff Robinson purchased an iPhone 16 from an Apple Store

11   located in Portland, Oregon.

12          14.     Plaintiff Robinson’s purchase of the iPhone 16 was motivated by Apple’s self-

13   promotion on Apple Intelligence integration and enhanced features with Siri which she believed would

14   improve her productivity with the phone.

15

16   B.     Defendant

17          15.     Apple Inc. is a California Corporation which, as noted above, has its principal place of

18   business in Cupertino, California.

19          16.     Apple designs, manufactures and sells the iPhone 16 series of cell phones in its stores
20   and online through its website and on other platforms.

21          17.     Apple is the developer of Apple Intelligence and Siri and has integrated them into

22   various products including the Apple iPhone 16.

23                                        JURISDICTION AND VENUE

24          18.     This Court has jurisdiction over the subject matter of this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C.

25   § 1332(d) because the amount in controversy for the Class (as defined below) exceeds $5,000,000

26   exclusive of interest and costs, there are more than 100 members of both the putative Class, and minimal

27   diversity exists because a significant portion of putative Class members are citizens of a state that is

28   not one of the states of which Defendant is a citizen.

                                          CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT
                                                    -2-
             Case 5:25-cv-04776-VKD            Document 1        Filed 06/05/25        Page 4 of 16




 1          19.     This Court has personal jurisdiction over Apple because its principal place of business

 2   is located in Cupertino, California and Apple markets its products, including the iPhone 16 that is the

 3   subject of this complaint, to California residents- including Plaintiff.

 4          20.     Venue is proper in the United States District Court for the Northern District of California

 5   pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(a)(1) and (c). A substantial part of the conduct giving rise to Plaintiff’s

 6   claims occurred in this District, Defendant regularly transacts business in this District, and Defendant

 7   has intentionally availed itself of the laws and markets within this District.

 8

 9                                    I.      GENERAL ALLEGATIONS

10   A. Apple as an Innovator

11          21.     Apple Computer Company was founded on April 1, 1976, by Steve Jobs, Steve

12   Wozniak, and Ronald Wayne in Cupertino, California. Their mission was to make computers accessible

13   and user-friendly for individuals and small businesses. One of the company's first product, the Apple

14   I, laid the groundwork for Apple's future in personal computing.

15          22.     In early January 2007, Apple introduced the iPhone that it promoted as a groundbreaking

16   device combining a mobile phone, an iPod, and an internet communicator into one product.

17          23.     Siri, Apple's intelligent voice assistant, originated from a project at SRI International's

18   Artificial Intelligence Center, funded by DARPA's CALO initiative. In 2007, this research led to the

19   formation of Siri Inc., which launched a standalone app in 2010. Apple acquired Siri Inc. shortly
20   thereafter, integrating the assistant into the iPhone 4S in 2011, marking a significant advancement in

21   voice-controlled technology.

22          24.     In June 2024, Apple announced "Apple Intelligence," as a suite of AI-powered features

23   integrated into iOS 18, iPadOS 18, and macOS Sequoia. This initiative aimed to enhance user

24   experience by providing personalized assistance through Siri and other applications 1.

25

26

27

 2   Intelligence2, Apple introduced "Apple Intelligence" as a suite of AI-driven features integrated into iOS

 3   18, iPadOS 18, and macOS Sequoia, aiming to enhance user experience across its devices. Here's a

 4   summary of the key features and enhancements:

 5                 a. Personalized AI Integration: Apple Intelligence combines generative models with

 6                    personal context to deliver relevant and useful intelligence across iPhone, iPad, and

 7                    Mac3.

 8                 b. Natural Interaction: Siri now offers more natural, flexible, and context-aware

 9                    interactions, maintaining context across multiple requests4.

10                 c. Text and Voice Input: Users can seamlessly switch between typing and speaking to

11                    Siri, enhancing accessibility and convenience 5.

12                 d. Expanded Knowledge: Siri can answer a broader range of questions about device

13                    features and settings, providing users with more comprehensive assistance 6.

14                 e. Systemwide Integration: Users can rewrite, proofread, and summarize text across

15                    various apps, including Mail, Notes, Pages, and third-party applications 7

16           26.      Consumers are increasingly prioritizing advanced AI capabilities when selecting

17   smartphones and electronic devices. AI-powered voice assistants like Siri are among the most valued

18   tools. Capitalizing on this trend, Apple has marketed its products by emphasizing AI features—

19   particularly to stay competitive with other major brands like Samsung and Google’s Android—despite
20   the representations being misleading or untrue.

21                                   II.      CLASS ACTION ALLEGATIONS

22           27.      Plaintiff brings this action, on behalf of herself and all others similarly situated, as a

23   class action pursuant to Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, Rule 23 (“Rule 23”).

 1          28.       Pursuant to Rule 23, Plaintiff seeks to represent a Nationwide Class composed of and

 2   defined as:

 3          The Class: During the fullest period allowed by law, all persons who purchased an Apple

 4          iPhone16 in the United States.

 5          29.       Excluded from the Class are the Defendants and its officers, directors, management,

 6   employees, subsidiaries, and affiliates. Also excluded from the Class are any district judge or magistrate

 7   judge to whom this case is assigned, as well as those judges’ immediate family members, judicial

 8   officers and their personnel, and all governmental entities.

 9          30.       Plaintiff reserves the right to revise or amend the above definitions and to add additional

10   Classes or Subclasses based on the discovery of new information.

11          31.       This action has been brought and may be properly maintained as a class action under

12   Federal Rule 23 because there is a well-defined community of interest in the litigation, the proposed

13   Class is easily ascertainable, and Plaintiff is a proper representative:

14          32.       Numerosity (Rule 23(a)(1)): The potential members of the proposed Class, as defined

15   and identified herein, are hundreds of thousands, if not millions, and so numerous that joinder of all

16   members of the Class or Subclass is impracticable.

17          33.       Typicality (Rule 23(a)(3)): Plaintiff Robinson’s claims, as purchaser of the Apple

18   iPhone16, are typical of the claims of the Class.

19          34.       Commonality: (Rule 23(a)(2)): Common questions of fact and law exist as to all
20   members of the Class and predominate over the questions affecting only individual members of the

21   Class. These common questions include but are not limited to:

22                 a. Whether Apple knew that the falsity of its claims concerning the capabilities of Apple

23                    Intelligence, Siri’s upgraded enhancements and their integration into the iPhone16 were

24                    false and/or misleading;

25                 b. Whether Apple knew that its promoted Apple Intelligence, Siri Upgrades and their

26                    integration into the iPhone 16 would justify a higher price when compared to the

27                    iPhone15;

28

 1                 c. Whether Apple was under a duty to Plaintiff, Class Members, and to disclose the true

 2                    nature and capabilities of Apple Intelligence, Siri and the AI capabilities of the

 3                    iPhone16;

 4                 d. Whether Apple benefited from selling an iPhone16 whose value was artificially inflated

 5                    by Apple’s concealment of the true features of the iPhone 16 cellphone at the time it

 6                    was sold to consumers;

 7                 e. Whether Apple engaged in unlawful, unfair, or deceptive business practices in

 8                    advertising and selling the iPhone16;

 9                 f. Whether Apple’s advertising and sales practices were false or deceptive;

10                 g. The amount by which Plaintiff and the Class overpaid for the iPhone16.

11           35.      Adequacy of Representation (Rule 23(a)(4)): Plaintiff will fairly and adequately

12   protect the interests of the Class, respectively. Plaintiff’s interests do not conflict with those of Class

13   Members, she has no conflict of interest with other Class Members, is not subject to any unique

14   defenses, and has retained competent and experienced counsel that has experience in complex

15   consumer protection class action cases, as well as sufficient financial and legal resources to prosecute

16   this case on behalf of the class. Plaintiff and counsel have no interest that is in conflict with or otherwise

17   antagonistic to the interests of other Class Members. Plaintiff and counsel are committed to vigorously

18   prosecuting this action on behalf of the members of the Class. Plaintiff and counsel anticipate no

19   difficulty in managing the litigation of this as a class action.
20           36.      Predominance and Superiority (Rule 23(b)(3)): In addition to satisfying the

21   prerequisites of Rule 23(a), Plaintiff satisfies the requirements for maintaining a class action under Rule

22   23(b)(3). Common questions of law and fact predominate over any questions affecting only individual

23   members of the Class, and a class action is superior to individual litigation and all other available

24   methods for the fair and efficient adjudication of this controversy. Here, common issues predominate

25   because liability can be determined on a class-wide basis even if some individualized damages

26   determination may be required. Individualized litigation also presents a potential for inconsistent or

27   contradictory judgments, and increases the delay and expense presented by complex legal and factual

28   issues of the case to all parties and the court system. Furthermore, the expense and burden of individual

                                           CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT

 1   litigation make it impossible for Class Members to individually redress the wrongs done to them and

 2   individual Class Members do not have a significant interest in controlling the prosecution of separate

 3   actions. By contrast, the class action device presents far fewer management difficulties and provides

 4   the benefits of a single adjudication, economy of scale, and comprehensive supervision by a single

 5   court. If this action is not certified as a class action, it will be impossible as a practical matter for many

 6   or most Class Members to bring individual actions to recover money from Defendant, due to the

 7   relatively small amounts of such individual recoveries relative to the costs and burdens of litigation.

 8   Plaintiff anticipates no difficulty in the management of this action which would preclude its

 9   maintenance as a class action.

10             37.   Plaintiff reserves the right to add representatives for the Class and/or future Subclass,

11   provided Defendant is afforded an opportunity to conduct discovery as to those representatives.

12                                              COUNT ONE

13     Violations Of California’s False And Misleading Advertising Law (“FAL”) Cal. Bus. &

14                                        Prof. Code, § 17500 et seq.

15             38.   Plaintiff repeats and re-alleges each and every allegation contained in all preceding

16   paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.

17             39.   Apple’s acts and practices, as described herein, have deceived and/or are likely to

18   continue to deceive class members and the public. Apple mispresented the Apple Intelligence

19   functionalities and capabilities, concealed delays in software rollout, and misrepresented the purpose

20   and extent of related iOS updates.

21             40.   By its actions, Apple disseminated uniform advertising regarding Apple Intelligence

22   based out of California and governed by California law. The advertising was, by its very nature, unfair,

23   deceptive, untrue, and misleading within the meaning of Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17500, et seq. Such

24   advertisements were intended to and likely did deceive the consuming public for the reasons detailed

25   herein.

26             41.   The above-described false, misleading, and deceptive advertising Apple disseminated

27   continues to have a likelihood to deceive in that Apple failed to disclose the true nature of Apple

28

 1   Intelligence’s functionality and related iOS software updates and rollouts, continuing to deceive

 2   consumers.

 3          42.     Apple continued to misrepresent to consumers that Apple Intelligence’s capabilities

 4   were fully operational and would be functional on the iPhone 16 Devices, even though they were not

 5   even fully developed. Had Apple disclosed this, rather than falsely advertising Apple Intelligence’s

 6   non-existent functionalities, consumers would not have purchased their iPhone 16 Devices or would

 7   not have purchased their iPhone 16 Devices for the premium prices that Apple charged.

 8          43.     In making and disseminating the statements alleged herein, Apple knew, or should have

 9   known, that its advertisements were untrue and misleading in violation of California law. Plaintiff and

10   other class members based their decisions to download iOS 15 on Apple’s omitted material facts.

11   Plaintiffs and class members were injured in fact and lost money and property as a result.

12          44.     The misrepresentations and non-disclosures by Apple of the material facts described and

13   detailed herein constitute false and misleading advertising and, therefore, constitute violations of Cal.

14   Bus. & Prof. Code § 17500, et seq.

15          45.     As a result of Apple’s wrongful conduct, Plaintiff and the class members have suffered

16   economic injury and other harm and seek damages, restitution and/or disgorgement, as appropriate.

17          46.     Monetary damages and other legal remedies alone are inadequate to address Apple’s

18   wrongful practices described in this complaint. Among other reasons, such remedies would not end

19   Apple’s wrongful practices. Plaintiff and Class Members are entitled to injunctive relief to address
20   Apple’s wrongful conduct. Plaintiff and Class Members further seek any additional equitable relief to

21   which they may be entitled.

22                                            COUNT TWO

23                   Violations Of California’s Unfair Competition Law (“UCL”)

24                                 Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code, § 17200 et seq.

25          47.     Plaintiff repeats and re-alleges each and every allegation contained in all preceding

26   paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.

27          48.     Apple is a “person” as defined by Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17201.

28

 1          49.       Apple violated the UCL by engaging in unlawful, unfair, and deceptive business acts

 2   and practices.

 3          50.       Apple has engaged in “unlawful” business practices by violating multiple laws,

 4   including the False and Misleading Advertising Law, Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17500, et seq.;

 5   California Legal Remedies Act (“CLRA”), Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1780, et seq.; and California common

 6   law.

 7          51.       Apple violated § 17200’s prohibition against “fraudulent” conduct by making

 8   misleading statements in its pervasive marketing and advertising of Apple Intelligence and the iPhone

 9   16 Products, regarding Apple Intelligence capabilities, without disclosing the critically important

10   information that the capabilities were not legitimate. Apple’s representations and omissions were likely

11   to mislead reasonable consumers and did mislead them. Plaintiff and other members of the Class relied

12   on Apple’s misrepresentations and would not have purchased iPhone 16 Devices, or would not have

13   paid such a premium price for the iPhone 16 Devices, if they knew that such promised capabilities

14   would not be delivered.

15          52.       Apple’s conduct is also “unfair” pursuant to the UCL. Apple’s conduct is substantially

16   injurious to consumers like Plaintiff and other Class Members, offends public policy, is immoral,

17   unethical, oppressive, and unscrupulous as the gravity of the conduct—Apple acted unfairly by

18   advertising and selling products while concealing the delay or non-existence of promised capabilities.

19   Apple engaged in this conduct at the expense of its consumers’ rights when other, lawful alternatives
20   were available—such as providing consumers with full information about the iPhone 16 Devices and

21   Apple Intelligence’s functionality, among other alternatives.

22          53.       As a result of Apple’s wrongful conduct, Plaintiff and Class Members have suffered

23   economic injury and other harm.

24          54.       Monetary damages and other legal remedies are inadequate to address Apple’s wrongful

25   practices described in this complaint. Among other reasons, such remedies would not end Apple’s

26   wrongful practices. Plaintiff is entitled to injunctive relief to address Apple’s wrongful conduct.

27   Plaintiff further seeks any additional equitable relief to which they may be entitled.

 2                              Fraud by Omission or Fraudulent Concealment

 3          55.      Plaintiff repeats and re-alleges each and every allegation contained in all preceding

 4   paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.

 5          56.      Plaintiff brings this cause of action on behalf of herself and the Class against Apple Inc.

 6          57.      Apple knew that its iPhone 16 lacked the technological capabilities it promoted

28   material in that a reasonable person would have considered them to be important in deciding whether

22           66.     Plaintiff brings this cause of action on behalf of herself and the Class against Apple Inc.

23           67.     Apple is the manufacturer, distributor, warrantor, and/or seller of the iPhone 16.

24           68.     The iPhone 16 cell phones were and are, at all relevant times, a “good(s)” within the

25   relevant laws. Apple knew or had reason to know of the specific uses for which the iPhone 16 cell

26   phones, as goods, were purchased.

27           69.     In addition to direct sales, Apple entered into agreements with retailers, suppliers,

28   and/or contractors to sell its iPhone 16 to be used by Plaintiff and other Class Members.

 1           70.     Apple provided Plaintiff and Class Members with implied warranties that the iPhone

 2   16’s were merchantable and fit for the ordinary purposes- which they promoted as advanced integration

 3   using Apple’s artificial intelligence platform, Apple Intelligence, and Siri for which they implied these

 4   technological advancements made this iPhone superior to previous generations of iPhones and superior

 5   to similar devices sold by their competitors. These implied warranties became part of the basis of the

 6   bargain between Plaintiff and Class Members and Igloo.

 7           71.     However, at the time of delivery, Apple breached the implied warranties because the

 8   iPhone 16 cell phones are not fit for their ordinary purpose of providing these advanced features as

 9   promoted. Therefore, these iPhone 16 cell phones contained a fundamental defect that rendered them

10   unfit for their ordinary purpose.

11           72.     As alleged herein, Plaintiff and Class Members purchased a product that was not

12   advanced as they were led to believe and paid a premium price for an inferior product.

13           73.     Since Apple also sold its iPhone 16 through third party vendors, Apple’s manifest intent

14   was that their warranties apply to Plaintiff and Class Members as third-party beneficiaries. Likewise, it

15   was reasonably foreseeable that Plaintiff and Class Members would be the intended beneficiaries of the

16   iPhone 16 and its warranties.

17           74.     Defendant breached the implied warranty of merchantability to Plaintiff and Class

18   Members in its representations that the iPhone 16 Devices contained the Apple Intelligence and Siri

19   capabilities that were advertised, when those representations were actually false.
20           75.     Apple failed to adequately warn or disclose to Plaintiff and other Class Members that

21   the iPhone 16 could not operate as promoted.

22           76.     Apple’s failure to adequately repair or replace the iPhone 16 caused the warranty to fail

23   in its essential purpose.

24           77.     As a direct and proximate result of the foregoing, Plaintiff and the Class Members

25   suffered, and continue to suffer, financial damage and injury, and are entitled to all damages, in addition

26   to costs, interest and fees, including attorneys’ fees, as allowed by law.

27                                                COUNT FIVE

28                                        Negligent Misrepresentation

 1          78.     Plaintiff repeats and re-alleges each and every allegation contained in all preceding

 2   paragraphs as though fully set forth herein.

 3          79.     Apple had a duty to Plaintiff and the class to exercise reasonable and ordinary care in

 4   the developing, marketing, and sale of Apple Intelligence and the iPhone 16 Devices.

 5          80.     Apple breached its duty to Plaintiffs and the class by falsely advertising and promoting

 6   Apple Intelligence and the capabilities that would be accessible on the iPhone 16 Devices, when such

 7   capabilities were not, and would not be, available.

 8          81.     Apple knew or should have known that the qualities and characteristics of the products

 9   were not as advertised, warranted and represented by Apple.

10          82.     As a result of Apple’s wrongful conduct, Plaintiffs and the class members have suffered

11   economic injury and other harm, as they would not have purchased the iPhone 16 Devices had they

12   known of the truth of Apple’s deceptions. Plaintiffs and the Class seek actual damages, attorney’s fees,

13   costs, and any other just and proper relief available.

15                                             Unjust Enrichment
